Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with clear sections (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Discussion, Conclusion). Ideas such as the per-sample Hessian trace proxy, H-E3 existence gate, and H-M1 mechanism gate are explicitly defined with equations (e.g., Tr(H_i^fc) ∝ ‖x_i‖² p_i(1−p_i)) and evaluation criteria. Tables (e.g., per-seed AUROC, confidence trajectories) and figures support the narrative. Minor issues include occasional dense technical language in the method section and references to unshown future experiments.

Novelty.justification: The work presents the first per-sample last-fc Hessian trace (K=50 Hutchinson via vmap+vjp) achieving AUROC≥0.85 on Waterbirds without group labels, extending LaBonte et al. [2024] group-level spectral results and LaBonte & Muthukumar [2026] Phase I/II theory to per-sample trajectories. However, the core contribution is incremental: it falsifies its own pre-registered confidence-differential mechanism and leaves the feature-norm channel unverified, with no new datasets, architectures, or downstream robustness improvements demonstrated.

Soundness.justification: Experimental protocol is rigorous: 5 seeds, explicit epoch-0 control (AUROC(t=0)∈[0.538,0.609]<0.70), Hutchinson CV<3% at K=50, and pre-registered gates. Code and logs confirm reproducibility of AUROC(t*)≥0.85 in 4/5 seeds and p_minority(t*)≥0.9678 (falsifying H-M1). Weaknesses include reliance on unverified feature-norm interpretation, training-set-only confidence measurements, and no direct penultimate-norm verification or DFR application, making conclusions about the surviving mechanism speculative.

Significance.justification: Addresses an important problem (annotation-free minority detection for spurious correlation robustness) and provides a second-order signal orthogonal to first-order proxies (JTT, SELF). However, practical impact is limited: the signal is not shown to improve worst-group accuracy via DFR-style retraining, generalization beyond ResNet-50/Waterbirds/95% spuriosity is untested, and the mechanism remains a candidate rather than verified. The dual result (existence without expected mechanism) is informative but does not yet yield deployable robustness gains.

strengths: Clear empirical existence result with strong controls (epoch-0 AUROC, Hutchinson stability) and reproducible code confirming AUROC≥0.85 in 4/5 seeds.
Principled falsification of the pre-registered confidence-differential mechanism with explicit per-seed trajectories and gate metrics.
weaknesses: Mechanism interpretation (feature-norm channel) is unverified; no direct measurement of ‖x_i‖² or downstream WGA improvement via the proxy.
Scope is narrow (single dataset/architecture) and the work does not demonstrate practical utility for annotation-free robustness, lowering overall impact.
